newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia, Britain co-operate on Olympic security.
newsitem.headline: Australia, Britain co-operate on Olympic security.

text.p: The Australian state government hosting the Sydney 2000 Olympics has signed an agreement with Britain to utilise British anti-terrorism experience to bolster security at the Games.
"There is no doubt that the British have accumulated quite a bit of expertise in security because of a 20-year experience with terrorism," said New South Wales state premier Bob Carr.
This year's Atlanta Olympics were marred by a bomb blast in July that killed two people and left more than 100 injured.
"They (the British) have specialist staff who can teach us things as we plan for the Olympics," Carr said in a radio interview from London broadcast here on Wednesday.

Under the agreement signed on Tuesday in London, New South Wales police will have access to hi-tech security techniques and devices, such as special night vision equipment, low light photography, microwave listening technology and British closed-circuit TV security systems.

In addition, police will be briefed on British expertise in screening cars for explosive devices, covert operations and perimeter intruder detection systems, security techniques refined during the conflict against the Irish Republican Army.
"We are ready to assist New South Wales to run the best ever Olympic Games," said the British Home Office in a statement released on the Internet.
